correctness.rationale: The proof reduces forcing to the exact white-neighbor counts \(q-\mathbf 1_{\{i\in J\}}\) and \(p-\mathbf 1_{\{i\in I\}}\), proves the two necessary obstructions, and supplies a legal first force for every remaining case with \(p,q\le2\). The enumerator follows by independent side omissions minus exactly the aligned \(2+2\) obstruction. A separate exhaustive verifier checks every subset for \(3\le n\le9\), including all coefficients and minima. The finite check is corroborative; no finite enumeration is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a classical dense bipartite family obtained by the minimal structured deletion of a perfect matching from \(K_{n,n}\). The result identifies exactly how that deletion changes zero forcing: among complements with at most two omissions per side, a single aligned-index obstruction is decisive. This drops the minimum from the complete-bipartite value \(2n-2\) to \(2n-4\), classifies every forcing set, and gives every coefficient of the polynomial. Because all zero forcing sets, not only the minimum, are used in propagation and throttling questions, the exact profile is a natural reusable invariant rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
